run.title: A sample requirement

roles.title: Product manager
roles.brief: Write the requirement in the README as numbered acceptance criteria AC-1, AC-2, ..., one sentence each and testable, into docs/product/acceptance.md.

roles.title: Architect
roles.brief: From the acceptance criteria, define the HTTP API contract (paths, requests, responses, error codes) in contracts/api.md, and the file layout of the backend, frontend, tests and ops in docs/architecture/layout.md.

roles.title: UI design
roles.brief: Design the structure and interaction of the home page, event detail page, sign-up form and list page in docs/design/pages.md; write a ready-to-use frontend/styles/main.css that also works well on a phone.

roles.title: Testing
roles.brief: Write tests from the acceptance criteria and the API contract, with node --test and zero dependencies. Put API tests in tests/api-*.test.js and page tests in tests/web-*.test.js (page tests read the files under frontend/ or call the frontend's pure functions; no browser), and project-level checks (npm scripts, ops/start.sh, Dockerfile: anything you can judge without starting the service) in tests/ops-*.test.js. The file name decides who a failing test is sent back to. Start each test name with the acceptance criterion's number, for example `AC-3: a full event cannot be joined`. API tests start backend/server.js themselves on a random port. The implementation is not written yet, so the tests should be red now; that is correct.

roles.title: Backend
roles.brief: Implement the backend as contracts/api.md says: the entry point is backend/server.js, which also serves frontend/ as static files; zero dependencies, data in memory. Make the API tests in tests/ pass.

roles.title: Frontend
roles.brief: Write the frontend pages as docs/design/pages.md and contracts/api.md say, getting data only through the HTTP API; use frontend/styles/main.css. A failed sign-up must show the reason.

roles.title: Operations
roles.brief: Write ops/start.sh (check the Node version, start the service, health check), a Dockerfile and a .dockerignore; the scripts in the root package.json are yours too: make sure `npm start` starts the service and `npm test` runs all the tests. Do not change other roles' directories.

roles.title: Review
roles.brief: Read-only: change no files. Look at the whole change of the run branch against the requirement commit and check it against docs/product/acceptance.md item by item: anything missing, any obvious defect, any change in another role's directory. On the first line of your last reply write `DONE: ready to deliver` or `DONE: changes needed`; if changes are needed, list each one and name the role it belongs to on a line such as `Send back: Backend`.

run.task_template:
[agent-rd-team run={run} role={role} branch={branch} worktree={worktree}]

You are the "{title}" on a development team. The team is building a small website; the other roles work at the same time in their own directories.

Requirement: {repo}/README.md (there is a copy in your working directory too).

Your working directory: {worktree} (git branch {branch}). Work only in this directory.
You may change only these paths: {writable}. Other directories belong to other roles: you may read them, not change them.

Read these upstream outputs first (if any): {inputs}

Your task: {brief}

When you are done:
1. In {worktree}, `git add` the files you changed and commit to {branch}; start the commit message with `[{role}]`.
2. Write `DONE: ` and a one-sentence summary on the first line of your last reply.
3. Do not push, do not touch other branches, do not change git config.
